factorRatings.note: Est. 1983, Razzi's runs a certified gluten-free kitchen alongside its regular menu, with four separate allergen-safe menus that Eater's gluten-free guide calls the holy grail of allergen-safe dining; hundreds of Yelp and Tripadvisor reviews describe consistently good food and generous portions rather than standout pizza craft specifically.

Reviewers on Yelp and Tripadvisor repeatedly single out the wood-fired crust as the thinnest and most delicate they've had, calling it some of the best pizza in the Pacific Northwest; prices run higher than most Seattle neighborhood shops.

An all-vegan pizzeria on Roosevelt Way with a devoted following; diners on HappyCow and Yelp call the crust the star of the show and the pizza the best vegan pizza they've ever had, with affordable, budget-friendly pricing.

The Seattle Times' review of the Mount Baker original describes thin, foldable crusts, ballooning edges and a bread-like chew, tracing owner Jeremy Hardy's pizza pedigree through Pizzeria Bianco, dough school, and time in Florence and Rome; Seattle Met has carried it on its business listings since it opened in 2006.

Fearless Critic scores Veraci's Neapolitan-style, applewood-fired slices 7.5/10 for food, tying for fifth among Seattle pizzerias at roughly $25 a person; the business grew out of a mobile wood-fired oven the founders built to sell pizza at the Ballard Farmers Market starting in 2004.
